claim_scope: Pushed arm64 macOS Cargo baseline plus bounded Apple MLX worker, device, tensor-fixture, and synthetic routed-MoE validation

workflow.name: macOS baseline
workflow.display_title: ci: add Apple MLX fixture validation

jobs.name: Apple Silicon workspace baseline

resource_observation.reason: The workflow asserted architecture and recorded the runner image, OS, and toolchain, but did not run hardware-capacity or disk-capacity probes. No capacity value is inferred from the hosted-runner label.

commands.exact_command:
uname -m
sw_vers
rustc -Vv
cargo -V
test "$(uname -m)" = arm64
commands.actual_result: The shell reported arm64; macOS 15.7.7 build 24G720; rustc 1.97.1; Cargo 1.97.1; the arm64 assertion passed.

commands.count_method: Summed every Cargo 'test result:' summary in the downloaded job log; the workflow itself did not run a separate --list command.

warnings: The inherited crates/quant/src/iq.rs unused_mut warning appeared during both workspace commands.
The inherited macOS serve target emitted 13 dead-code warnings during both workspace commands.

resource_observation.reason: This was a small-fixture correctness job. It did not probe or benchmark hosted-runner capacity.

environment_boundary.uploaded_artifact_note: The generated temporary JSON records were asserted during the job but were not uploaded or retained as workflow artifacts.

commands.exact_command:
test "$(uname -m)" = arm64
sw_vers
test -z "$PULSARMLX_MODEL_GGUF"
test -f uv.lock
test -f fixtures/mlx/manifest.json
test -f fixtures/mlx/routed-moe-v1.json
test -f docs/validation/mlx-device-smoke.json
test -f docs/validation/mlx-tensor-fixtures.json
test -f docs/validation/synthetic-moe-v1.json
commands.actual_result: The arm64, empty-model-variable, lockfile, fixture, and prerequisite-evidence assertions passed.

commands.exact_command:
uv python install 3.12.13
uv sync --frozen --python 3.12.13
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import platform
from importlib.metadata import version

assert platform.machine() == "arm64"
assert version("mlx") == "0.32.0"
assert version("mlx-metal") == "0.32.0"
PY
commands.actual_result: CPython 3.12.13, mlx 0.32.0, and mlx-metal 0.32.0 were installed from the frozen environment and the version/architecture assertions passed.
1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 11 filtered out; finished in 0.45 seconds.

commands.exact_command: cargo run -p mlx-backend --bin pulsar-mlx -- validate-fixtures --manifest fixtures/mlx/manifest.json --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/mlx-tensor-fixtures.json"
commands.actual_result: Seven evaluated MLX fixture cases passed.

commands.exact_command: cargo run -p mlx-backend --bin pulsar-mlx -- validate-synthetic-moe --fixture fixtures/mlx/routed-moe-v1.json --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/synthetic-moe-v1.json"
commands.actual_result: The evaluated synthetic routed-MoE fixture passed.

commands.exact_command:
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"])
tensor = json.loads((root / "mlx-tensor-fixtures.json").read_text())
synthetic = json.loads((root / "synthetic-moe-v1.json").read_text())
assert tensor["status"] == "passed"
assert tensor["case_count"] == 7
assert synthetic["status"] == "passed"
assert synthetic["fixture_kind"] == "synthetic"
assert synthetic["fallback_used"] is False
assert os.environ.get("PULSARMLX_MODEL_GGUF", "") == ""
PY
commands.actual_result: Generated tensor and synthetic records reported passed; seven tensor cases were present; the synthetic record had no fallback; the external-model variable remained empty.

The standard hosted runner's CPU count, CPU model, unified-memory capacity, and available disk were not measured, so this record makes no capacity or local-M1-Ultra equivalence claim.
No complete expert, complete layer, checkpoint routing, attention, logits, generation, giant-model execution, production serving, performance benchmark, Linux runtime, or CUDA runtime was exercised.
The fixture job proves only its committed small deterministic cases on the recorded arm64 runner and dependency versions.

GitHub job success establishes the recorded commands on the recorded hosted runner, not performance or broad model compatibility.
